hero: In a provincial hospital nursery in Cagayan Valley, a Filipino pediatric nephrologist gently examines the abdomen of a newborn Filipino boy in an incubator while his young parents, the father in a farmer's cap, watch closely and a nurse holds an ultrasound printout; soft daylight, tender and hopeful mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Urinary tract dilation is graded by pelvic diameter, gestational age and associated findings.
figures.content: Two panels. Left 'Antenatal': A1 'APRPD 4 to <7 mm (16–27 wk) or 7 to <10 mm (≥28 wk)'; A2–3 '≥7 mm or ≥10 mm, or calyces, parenchyma, ureter, bladder, low fluid'. Right 'Postnatal (scan after 48 hours)': P1 '10 to <15 mm'; P2 '≥15 mm or peripheral calyces'; P3 'abnormal parenchyma, ureter or bladder'. Kidney cross-section icons showing increasing dilation. Footer: 'Seen in 1–2% of fetuses'.

figures.teaches: The first year of a boy with valves follows six steps.
figures.content: Six steps in a curved line: 1 'Drain' (catheter now); 2 'Measure' (creatinine, sodium, weight); 3 'Image' (ultrasound, voiding study); 4 'Relieve' (valve ablation); 5 'Track' (nadir creatinine year 1; cut-off '1 mg/dL'); 6 'Protect' (salt and water, infection, bladder, growth). Side box: 'Meta-analysis: CKD 37.9%, kidney failure 13.6%'.
